title: How to replace the Dishwasher Circulation Pump
safety: Turn off power at the breaker
steps: Disconnect power at the breaker and shut off the water supply.
Remove the toe-kick panel and place a towel under the unit.
Disconnect the drain hose and water line if needed to pull the dishwasher out.
Access the pump from the bottom panel; take a photo of wiring and hose positions.
Disconnect wiring harness and loosen hose clamps.
Remove mounting fasteners and lift out the circulation pump.
Install the new pump, reattach hoses and wiring, and check seals.
Reassemble panels, restore water and power, and run a short test cycle to check for leaks.

title: How to replace the Dishwasher Drain Pump
safety: Turn off power at the breaker
steps: Turn off power at the breaker and shut off the water supply.
Remove the toe-kick panel and place a towel under the front of the dishwasher.
If needed, pull the dishwasher forward for access (disconnect water line/drain hose only if necessary).
Access the pump from the bottom; take a photo of wiring and hose routing before removal.
Disconnect the pump wiring connector.
Release hose clamp(s) and remove the drain hose from the pump.
Remove mounting fasteners or rotate/unlock the pump (depending on design) and remove it.
Install the new drain pump, reconnect hoses and wiring, and reassemble panels.
Restore water and power, then run a short rinse/drain cycle to confirm proper draining and check for leaks.

title: How to replace the Dishwasher Heating Element
safety: Turn off power at the breaker
Allow the element to cool completely
steps: Turn off power at the breaker and shut off the water supply.
Open the dishwasher and remove the lower rack for working space.
Remove the lower access panel/toe-kick and place a towel under the unit.
From underneath, locate the heating element terminals and note wire placement (take a photo).
Disconnect the wires from the element terminals.
Loosen the mounting nuts that hold the element in place.
From inside the tub, carefully lift and remove the heating element.
Install the new element with the same orientation, tighten the mounting nuts, and reconnect wires.
Reassemble panels, restore water and power, and run a short cycle to check for leaks and proper heating.

title: How to replace the Dishwasher Door Latch Assembly
safety: Turn off power at the breaker
steps: Turn off power at the breaker.
Open the dishwasher door and remove the screws around the inner door panel.
Separate the inner panel carefully and support the control panel/wiring as needed.
Locate the door latch assembly at the top of the door; take a photo of wiring connections.
Disconnect the latch wiring connector(s).
Remove mounting screws/clips and remove the old latch assembly.
Install the new latch assembly, reconnect wiring, and ensure the latch engages smoothly.
Reattach the inner door panel and reinstall all screws.
Restore power and test that the door closes securely and the dishwasher starts normally.

title: How to replace the Refrigerator Water Inlet Valve
safety: Shut off the household water supply
steps: Unplug the refrigerator and shut off the household water supply.
Pull the refrigerator away from the wall for access and place a towel under the valve area.
Remove the rear lower access panel to expose the water inlet valve.
Take a photo of tubing and wire connections before disconnecting anything.
Disconnect the wire harness(es) from the valve solenoids.
Release the water line(s) from the valve (use the correct method for the fitting type).
Remove mounting screws and remove the old inlet valve.
Install the new valve, reconnect water line(s) and wiring, and reattach the access panel.
Turn water back on and check for leaks, then plug the refrigerator back in and verify water/ice operation.

title: How to replace the Refrigerator Water Filter
safety: Follow the filter housing instructions for your model
steps: Locate the water filter housing (inside the fridge compartment or at the base grille, depending on model).
Place a towel under the filter area to catch drips.
Remove the old filter by turning/pulling it out according to the housing design.
Insert the new filter and lock it into place.
Run water through the dispenser for several minutes to purge air and flush the filter (if your model has a dispenser).
Reset the filter indicator light (if present).

title: How to replace the Refrigerator Ice Maker Assembly
safety: Turn off the ice maker and water supply if applicable
steps: Unplug the refrigerator (or turn off power at the breaker).
Turn off the ice maker (switch OFF / raise shutoff arm).
Remove the ice bin/bucket for access.
Remove mounting screws securing the ice maker assembly and gently pull it forward.
Disconnect the wiring harness connector.
Install the new ice maker assembly and reconnect the wiring harness.
Reinstall mounting screws and return the ice bin/bucket.
Restore power and turn the ice maker back ON. Allow up to 24 hours for ice production to normalize.

title: How to replace the Refrigerator Evaporator Fan Motor
steps: Unplug the refrigerator.
Remove items and shelves from the freezer compartment as needed for access.
Remove the rear freezer panel to access the evaporator area (take care with any wiring).
Locate the evaporator fan motor and take a photo of wiring connections.
Disconnect the fan wiring connector and remove mounting screws/clips.
Remove the old fan motor and install the new motor in the same position.
Reconnect wiring, reinstall the rear panel, and return shelves/items.
Plug the refrigerator back in and confirm the fan runs and airflow returns.

title: How to replace the Refrigerator Thermistor (Temperature Sensor)
steps: Unplug the refrigerator.
Access the thermistor location (often behind an interior panel in the fridge or freezer compartment).
Remove any panel/cover screws and carefully open the panel.
Locate the thermistor and take a photo of how it’s mounted and connected.
Disconnect the thermistor connector and remove it from its clip/housing.
Install the new thermistor in the same position and reconnect the connector.
Reinstall panels/covers and restore power.
Allow several hours for temperatures to stabilize and verify normal cooling behavior.
